cases.name: Kara Welsh
cases.about:
She was a University of Wisconsin-Whitewater gymnast. he won the national title on the vault last year at the National Collegiate Gymnastics Association Championship and was majoring in business management.

The university’s athletics department called Welsh a “phenom on the vault” who “excelled” in “high-pressure situations,” noting she held four of the top eight scores recorded for the vault in the school’s gymnastics program history.

“To put into words the impact Kara had on the Warhawk community is impossible,” said Jennifer Regan, the head coach of women’s gymnastics at UW-Whitewater. “A powerful athlete, dedicated teammate, and the light in everyone’s dark days, Kara truly lifted each and every one of us up in her time as a Warhawk gymnast. There are no words to describe the void we all feel in our hearts, but Kara’s legacy will live on through Warhawk gymnastics forever.”

Welsh’s older sister, Kaeli, spoke at the bond hearing, telling the court Kara was “a friend to everyone” and “the light of my life.”

Her obituary siad, "Kara grew up in Plainfield, IL and attended Indian Trail Middle School and Plainfield Central High School, class of 2021. She went on to attend the University of Wisconsin Whitewater in Whitewater WI, where she studied Business Management.

Kara was a talented and devoted gymnast. She competed for Aspire Gymnastics Academy in vault, bars, beam, and floor. In 2021, she competed for Region 5 at Nationals. At college she competed in vault and floor, winning a regional and national title in 2023, as well as an additional regional title in 2024.

Kara enjoyed making people laugh, lifting weights, and being a collegiate gymnast.

Kara will be remembered as a warm and loving woman who made friends everywhere she went. She will be deeply missed by her many friends and family. The world will be a darker place without her presence."
